title: KV: Lighthouse evictor and memory-tiling allocator to reduce fragmentation and spill jitter
author: Priya Raman
release_notes: Introduces the Lighthouse evictor and a memory-tiling allocator for KV cache; reduces fragmentation, smooths spillover, and improves tail-latency under mixed workloads. Backwards-compatible API. Notable perf: 18-35% reduction in spill-triggered P99 under mixed read/write tenancy.
description: Summary: This PR implements 'Lighthouse', a fragmentation-aware eviction policy with a time-decayed residency score, and pairs it with a memory-tiling allocator that reduces internal fragmentation and makes spill decisions more deterministic. Motivation: production workloads showed intermittent spikey spill behavior caused by small fragmented free regions and tenant-locality churn. Existing LRU-style approaches could prematurely evict recently-prefetched segments when fragmentation forced large contiguous reservations to spill. The goal is to reduce spill jitter, stabilize tail latency, and improve predictable residency for multi-tenant serving. Key ideas: 1) Lighthouse evictor computes a per-segment residency score that combines: hotness (time-decayed access frequency), write-pressure penalty (recent writes raise cost), and fragmentation penalty (favoring larger contiguous spans). The policy uses tenant-weighted aging to avoid eviction starvation for low-traffic tenants. 2) Memory-tiling allocator divides the KV arena into tiles of configurable sizes (default 4MB/256KB/32KB buckets) and prefers placement that keeps hot working sets within few tiles to minimize cross-tile eviction churn. 3) Paged-spill attenuator adds hysteresis to spill triggers: soft-spill threshold and a progressive spill ramp reduce aggressive full-arena spill events by spilling lower-priority tiles first and coalescing small spill candidates into larger batched spill operations to improve throughput. 4) Kernel/scheduler hints: the allocator exposes lightweight placement hints to the kernel selector so continuous-batching can align batch composition with tile locality (reduces remote KV misses during decoding). 5) Compatibility and controls: runtime flags for soft_reserve_pct, spill_ramp_ms, tile_sizes, and per-tenant residency weights. Includes telemetry hooks for fragmentation_score, tile_evictions, and spill_coalesced_bytes. Changes in this PR: Commits: - 7e3d2b5: initial lighthouse evictor skeleton and unit tests. - cb12a8f: memory-tiling allocator core (C++), allocator APIs, and tiled free list. - a1d9f40: spill attenuator and spill-ramp logic; integration with tile allocator. - f5c6b2e: kernel selector hints and batching alignment changes in scheduler. - 19b8ef3: docs and perf bench harness; added integration tests and CI benchmarks. Files changed (high-level): - src/kv/cache/lighthouse_evictor.rs: new eviction policy implementation and telemetry hooks. - src/kv/cache/tiling_allocator.cpp/.h: allocator core, tile metadata, and allocation algorithms. - runtime/scheduler/batching_controller.go: uses tile locality hints to form continuous batches. - runtime/kernels/kernel_selector.cc: small API to accept tile-locality hints and prefer kernels that preserve cache locality. - bench/perf/kv_tiling_bench.py: microbench harness showing mixed-tenant workload. - tests/kv/evictor_integration_test.go: added scenarios for fragmentation and tenant isolation. - docs/design/kv-lighthouse.md: design rationale and tuning guide. Implementation notes: - Evictor: Lighthouse maintains a compact residency table per tile with epoch-based decays so updates are lock-free in the fast path. It favors evicting from tiles with the highest fragmentation_score*resident_weight product. The eviction loop uses a two-tier candidate sampler (fast local sampler + background compactor pass) to avoid long stalls. - Allocator: The tiling allocator keeps per-size freelists and a small in-memory bitmap to locate contiguous spans for large reservations. When a large reservation fails, it triggers a background coalesce that attempts to defragment adjacent free tiles asynchronously. - Spill attenuator: Uses a configurable soft threshold (default 72% arena usage) and a hard threshold (default 90%). When soft threshold crossed, the attenuator will attempt selective spill of low-priority tiles and schedule coalesce; only when hard threshold reached will it perform aggressive immediate spill. - Scheduler/kernel hints: The runtime scheduler includes a new small hint in request metadata indicating preferred tile id(s). Kernel selector tries to keep KV-affine sequences on the same device-local state. Tests and benchmarks: - Unit tests for scoring math, eviction eligibility, and tile allocator correctness. - Integration test that reproduces the production fragmentation scenario (high churn of small writes across tenants) and validates that Lighthouse reduces spill events. - Benchmarks show 18% reduction in P99 spill latency under mixed-tenancy writes and up to 35% reduction in spill-related P99 under heavy write bursts. - Microbench shows ~4% CPU overhead in maintenance background tasks at default config. Review thread (high-level): - Jonah Keene (reviewer): requested clarifications on concurrency safety in the residency table and asked for a microbenchmark that reproduces eviction loop tail behavior. Author response: added epoch-based lock-free updates and a microbench harness showing stable latencies; updated description and tests. - Marcel Duarte: noted potential memory pressure during coalesce and asked for a configurable backoff; added spill_ramp_ms and retired the immediate coalesce on low-memory signals. - Aisha Beg: asked for telemetry naming conventions and alerting suggestions; added prom metrics kv_lighthouse_fragmentation_score and kv_tile_spill_count and documented alert thresholds. CI and validation: - CI initially failed a flaky test in evictor_integration_test (race in test harness). Fixed by increasing test harness timeout and improving deterministic seeds; CI rerun passed. - Bench CI (perf job) reported the expected delta and attached profiling artifacts. Risk and rollout plan: - This is opt-in behind runtime flag; no migration needed for existing tenants. Default config is conservative (soft thresholds tuned to production baseline). Rollout plan: enable in canary cluster for 24-48 hours with spike protection, monitor fragmentation_score and tile_evictions dashboards, then gradual ramp to 20% of traffic, evaluate, and full rollout. Observability additions: - New Prometheus metrics: kv_lighthouse_fragmentation_score, kv_tile_evictions_total, kv_spill_coalesced_bytes, kv_spill_ramp_activations. - Grafana dashboard panels included in docs/design/kv-lighthouse.md. Performance notes and caveats: - Works best for workloads where hot keys are co-located; pathological uniformly-random small writes still benefit but less so. - Background coalesce is best-effort and may be throttled under memory pressure; UI settings allow manual compaction windows. - Continuous-batching alignment reduces KV misses but requires the scheduler to be batch-aware; added a compatibility shim to disable hints per model if necessary. Related work: builds on prior spill-coalescer and slab compactor efforts but focuses on combining fragmentation-aware scoring with placement-level tiling to avoid repeated small spills. Also complements kernel-level batching improvements by keeping working sets localized. Deployment and follow-ups: - Follow-up work: adaptive tile resizing based on observed fragmentation patterns and tenant-specific residency tuning via the Optimize recommendations engine. - Proposed Linear tasks: ENG-5028 (tile adaptive resizing), ENG-5032 (Optimize integration for residency tuning). Merge outcome: squash-merged after approvals and green CI. Notes: no API breaking changes in public SDKs; all knobs are runtime flags and documented.
